stories.title: 47 university students attend first Unmute Yo’Self public speaking event in Accra
stories.summary: Forty-seven university students have participated in the first edition of Unmute Yo’Self, a free public speaking and confidence-building event aimed at helping young people communicate their ideas more effectively. The event was held on Friday, October 23, 2026, at the Accra AI Community Center in Ridge, Accra.

articles.title: 47 university students attend first Unmute Yo’Self public speaking event in Accra
articles.excerpt: Forty-seven university students have participated in the first edition of Unmute Yo’Self, a free public speaking and confidence-building event aimed at helping young people communicate their ideas more effectively. The event was held on Friday, October 23, 2026, at the Accra AI Community Center in Ridge, Accra. Organised by the Sincerely Accra Podcast in collaboration with The Gold Coast Report (GCR), the programme was sponsored by Malta Guinness and Ashesi University. Participants included students from first year through to their final year. The initiative was designed to address the challenges young people face in expressing themselves confidently in classrooms, job interviews and professional settings.

stories.title: GRASAG president calls for sustainable funding for agricultural research in Africa
stories.summary: The President of the Graduate Students Association of Ghana (GRASAG), Richard Class-Peters, has called for sustainable financing for agricultural research to improve food security, boost local production and support economic growth across Africa.

articles.title: GRASAG president calls for sustainable funding for agricultural research in Africa
articles.excerpt: The President of the Graduate Students Association of Ghana (GRASAG), Richard Class-Peters, has called for sustainable financing for agricultural research to improve food security, boost local production and support economic growth across Africa. He made the call at the recently concluded World Bank’s Africa Growth and Opportunity – Research in Action (AGORA) 2026 conference in Palermo, Italy. Mr Class-Peters said African countries must increase investment in research and innovation while strengthening farmer cooperatives to improve agricultural productivity and build more resilient food systems. “Sustainable financing for agricultural research is critical to empowering innovation, strengthening farmer cooperatives and transforming local agriculture for food security and economic prosperity in Africa,” he said.

articles.excerpt: Former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has called for mandatory fingerprint background checks as a condition for teacher licensing, arguing that stronger vetting is needed to prevent individuals with relevant criminal records from working in schools. He has also proposed establishing a sex offenders register that would be checked against the fingerprints of teachers and other education workers before they are allowed to work in public or private schools. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse, Dr Adutwum questioned the effectiveness of existing background checks, claiming that the current teacher licensing process does not adequately establish whether applicants have criminal records.

stories.title: Adutwum proposes criminal sanctions for teachers who fail to report child abuse
stories.summary: Former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has called for mandatory reporting laws requiring teachers, medical professionals and other relevant professionals to report suspected child sexual abuse, with criminal sanctions for those who fail to do so.

articles.title: Adutwum proposes criminal sanctions for teachers who fail to report child abuse
articles.excerpt: Former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has called for mandatory reporting laws requiring teachers, medical professionals and other relevant professionals to report suspected child sexual abuse, with criminal sanctions for those who fail to do so. He argues that Ghana’s current system relies too heavily on the Ghana Education Service (GES) to handle abuse cases, making stronger legal obligations and enforcement necessary to protect students. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse, Dr Adutwum said reporting suspected abuse should be a legal duty rather than a matter of personal discretion. “As a medical doctor who gets wind of this, a child comes and you know that he has been abused, it's not optional for you to say I'm not reporting. A teacher who observes something going on, it's not optional. You have to report. So it becomes part of the law,” he said.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, and signed by General Secretary Fifi Fiavi Kwetey, the party said its Functional Executive Committee (FEC) took the decision after further consideration. “FEC has directed that Mr Zakaria Abdulai step aside, in the overriding interest of transparency and accountability, to allow for an unhindered investigation by the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service,” the statement said.

articles.excerpt: Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has vowed that the sexual abuse allegations at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) will not be allowed to fade from public attention without a resolution. Speaking at a press conference in Accra on Monday, October 26, 2026, the Minister said the case would not follow the pattern of other major public controversies that attract intense media attention before gradually disappearing from the national conversation. “Amid the calls from various sections of society for a full-scale investigation of similar malpractices in other educational institutions in the country, this scandal won't suffer the same fate as other burning issues which are normal to be discussed with gusto in the media over a period and then go out with a whimper. That won't happen in respect of this matter,” he said.

articles.title: GTEC directs Ghana’s public universities to reopen by October 16 and begin lectures on October 19
articles.excerpt: The Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) has directed all public universities to reopen their campuses for the 2026/2027 academic year by Friday, October 16, despite any earlier decisions to postpone reopening. In a letter dated October 13, 2026, and signed by Deputy Director-General Prof. Augustine Ocloo on behalf of the Director-General, the Commission said academic activities, particularly lectures, must commence on Monday, October 19. GTEC has also directed university managements to ensure that halls of residence, academic libraries, departmental registration desks and other essential student support facilities are fully staffed and operational by Thursday, October 15.

articles.excerpt: Ensign Global University and the University of Utah have graduated 20 entrepreneurs from the second cohort of the Master of Business Creation (MBC) programme, an initiative designed to help business owners strengthen their enterprises and create employment opportunities. The programme takes a practical approach to entrepreneurship education, allowing participants to apply lessons in areas such as marketing, financial projections and human resource management directly to their businesses. President of Ensign Global University, Professor Stephen Alder, said the initiative could help address Africa’s employment challenges by equipping graduates to create jobs rather than rely solely on existing vacancies.

articles.title: EchoHouse founders Beryl and Bright Agyekum-Ayaaba graduate as joint valedictorians
articles.excerpt: Nearly two decades after turning a university magazine into EchoHouse, a marketing agency operating in eight countries, married founders Beryl Agyekum-Ayaaba and Bright Mamud-Ayaaba have reached another milestone in their journey together, graduating as joint valedictorians from a Master of Business Creation programme. Together since 2006 and married for 10 years, the couple has built their business and personal lives in tandem, learning to balance marriage, parenthood, entrepreneurship and academic demands while growing EchoHouse from a campus idea into an international company. For Bright, sharing the honour with his wife was both surreal and deeply personal.

articles.title: UG commissions Alex A. Dadey Centre in honour of Dr Alexander Apau Dadey Snr, Father of KGL Boss
articles.excerpt: The University of Ghana (UG) has commissioned the Alex A. Dadey Centre at its Legon campus in honour of Dr Alexander Apau Dadey Snr., a veteran educationist and administrator whose career spanned teaching, institutional leadership and public service. The facility was commissioned on Friday, October 23, 2026, in a partnership between the University and the University of Ghana Alumni Association (UGAA). To ensure its long-term sustainability, the KGL Foundation has committed to funding the centre for the next 20 years. Speaking at the ceremony, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ghana, Professor Nana Aba Appiah Amfo, said Dr Dadey Snr. was a former student of the University who later served on its governing council from 1978 to 1985.

stories.title: GES directs schools to enforce the Code of Conduct’s ban on students doing chores at teachers’ bungalows
stories.summary: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has directed all senior high schools to immediately comply with an existing provision in its Code of Conduct that prohibits students from performing household chores at the bungalows of teachers and headteachers.

articles.title: GES directs schools to enforce the Code of Conduct’s ban on students doing chores at teachers’ bungalows
articles.excerpt: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has directed all senior high schools to immediately comply with an existing provision in its Code of Conduct that prohibits students from performing household chores at the bungalows of teachers and headteachers. The Service says the practice, which is already prohibited under the Code of Conduct, must stop with immediate effect. GES Director-General, Professor Ernest Kofi Davis, gave the directive in an interview with JoyNews' Naa Dedei Tettey on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Professor Davis explained that the Code of Conduct, under Section 3.7 V, explicitly states that students are not expected to be asked to engage in household chores.

articles.title: Ministry of Education creates direct reporting channels for sexual abuse complaints after Obuasi SHTS case
articles.excerpt: The Ministry of Education is creating direct reporting channels, including a hotline, to allow students, parents, teachers and community members to report sexual abuse in schools without having to go through head teachers or other local authorities who may be implicated. Deputy Education Minister Dr Clement Apaak disclosed this on JoyNews’ News Night on Thursday, October 22, 2026, saying the allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) had exposed weaknesses in the existing reporting structure. “In the wake of this issue, we became aware that there was a challenge within the reporting structure as far as GES is concerned,” he said.

stories.title: Sex therapist calls for national sexuality education policy in Ghana
stories.summary: A US-trained sex therapist, Joshua Kwame Yeboah, has called on the government and stakeholders to develop a national sexuality education policy to address gaps in public understanding and strengthen professional practice in Ghana.

articles.title: Sex therapist calls for national sexuality education policy in Ghana
articles.excerpt: A US-trained sex therapist, Joshua Kwame Yeboah, has called on the government and stakeholders to develop a national sexuality education policy to address gaps in public understanding and strengthen professional practice in Ghana. Mr Yeboah, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of the Institute of Sexuality, Marriage and Family Life Research and Training (iSMART), said sexuality remained difficult to discuss constructively in many homes, schools, churches and communities. “In some homes, schools, churches and communities, sexuality remains too uncomfortable to discuss constructively. Young people may be warned against sexual activity without being adequately equipped to understand puberty, personal boundaries, consent, abuse prevention and responsible decision-making,” he said.

articles.title: Protect vulnerable girls, not GES reputation – Dr Kwabena Tandoh
articles.excerpt: Former Deputy Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES), Dr Kwabena B. Tandoh, has urged educational leaders to prioritise protecting vulnerable girls in schools rather than focus on safeguarding the reputation of the service and other educational institutions. Speaking on The Pulse with Faustina Sarfo, he said allegations of abuse exposed through documentaries should prompt a broader examination of the systems responsible for protecting children in schools. “I think I first need to state clearly that our responsibility as educational leaders is not to protect the GES or educational institutions, but to protect the vulnerable girls who sit in our classrooms,” he said.

stories.title: Protecting Ghana’s Students: Is the Time Right to revisit the case for Comprehensive Sexuality Education in our schools?
stories.summary: When students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School vented their anger on campus in August this year, damaging property and forcing the school to close, many of us saw only indiscipline.

articles.title: Protecting Ghana’s Students: Is the Time Right to revisit the case for Comprehensive Sexuality Education in our schools?
articles.excerpt: When students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School vented their anger on campus in August this year, damaging property and forcing the school to close, many of us saw only indiscipline. Look a little closer, and a more troubling picture appears: young people who, by several accounts, had been trying for months to be heard. At least 19 female students have accused their headmaster of sexual abuse over the past year, according to an investigation by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni. The Ghana Education Service interdicted him on 14th October, and on 20th October, the Interior Minister told Parliament that he had been arrested and that DNA evidence was being pursued.

articles.excerpt: An NPP-aligned group in the Ashanti Region has called for an independent investigation into allegations of misconduct involving the Headmaster of Obuasi Senior High School, Zakaria Abdulai, citing concerns about student safety and the credibility of the inquiry. articles.excerpt: Sustainable Impact Makers International (SIMI) says its 2026 Health Equity Summit reached more than 1,000 people in the Bono Region, combining community advocacy, health education and preventive services to address barriers to healthcare access. The three-day initiative, held in Sunyani from July 23 to 25 under the theme “Health Equity in Action: From Periods to Parenthood, For All,” recorded more than 420 screening encounters across 13 service categories and completed over 500 National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) registrations. About 800 secondary school students also participated in a film screening and facilitated discussion on issues including menstrual health, consent, early marriage and school retention.

articles.title: Who protects the dreamer? (Part II) — Reflections on the vulnerability of the Girl Child in the Obuasi Senior High Technical School Scandal
articles.excerpt: There is something sickeningly cruel about a society that encourages a girl to dream, sends her to school to build that dream, and then leaves her vulnerable to the very people entrusted with protecting her. If established, these allegations would represent not merely a crime, but a monstrous betrayal of trust, authority and the sacred responsibility of educating children.

stories.title: From shock to action: Protecting our children from sexual abuse
stories.summary: I wish to commend Manasseh Azure for his documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow, which has brought renewed attention to the disturbing reality of sexual abuse in our secondary schools.

articles.title: From shock to action: Protecting our children from sexual abuse
articles.excerpt: I wish to commend Manasseh Azure for his documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow, which has brought renewed attention to the disturbing reality of sexual abuse in our secondary schools. May I confess that, as a researcher who has conducted extensive studies on child sexual abuse in Ghana, I have not yet gathered the courage to watch the documentary because of how horrifying and distressing the story is. Although it has shocked many Ghanaians and left others speechless, I fear that what it reveals may only be the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the reality of child sexual abuse in our society. Many children are abused in places where they should feel safest, including their schools and homes. Sadly, some are abused by the very people entrusted with their care and protection. Perpetrators may include teachers, relatives, domestic workers, strangers, and others who exploit children's vulnerability and trust.

articles.excerpt: Ghana’s response to urban flooding may depend partly on what future engineers learn in the classroom, with a university-led project calling for sustainable drainage systems to become part of construction education. Pro Vice-Chancellor of the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development (USTED), and project lead, Professor Isaac Boateng, says engineers must be trained to do more than construct drains as the country confronts the pressures of urban expansion, intense rainfall and inadequate stormwater management. “The question is no longer simply whether we can construct drains. stories.summary: The University Basic School (UBS), Legon, has won the 2026 Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)-Food Research Institute Quiz Competition, securing its third consecutive title with 70 points.

articles.title: University Basic School, Legon, wins CSIR quiz for third consecutive year
articles.excerpt: The University Basic School (UBS), Legon, has won the 2026 Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)-Food Research Institute Quiz Competition, securing its third consecutive title with 70 points. UBS finished ahead of Christ the King International School, which scored 63 points, The Ridge Church School with 50 points, and Armed Forces Basic School with 47 points. The competition was held at the CSIR-Food Research Institute's conference hall at Shiashie in Accra as part of activities to commemorate World Food Day, observed annually on October 16. The latest victory extends UBS's winning streak since it first participated in the competition in 2024, having also emerged champion in the 2024 and 2025 editions.

stories.title: Educated but unable to communicate? The missing link in Ghana’s University education
stories.summary: Imagine a university graduate attending a job interview with an impressive academic record. The applicant demonstrates knowledge of the discipline studied but struggles to explain ideas clearly.

articles.title: Educated but unable to communicate? The missing link in Ghana’s University education
articles.excerpt: Imagine a university graduate attending a job interview with an impressive academic record. The applicant demonstrates knowledge of the discipline studied but struggles to explain ideas clearly. When asked to write a short report, the sentences are poorly constructed, the paragraphs lack coherence, and the intended message becomes difficult to understand. Does this mean the graduate is not knowledgeable? Certainly not. However, it raises an important question: Are our universities paying sufficient attention to students' ability to communicate what they know?* University education should do more than produce graduates with certificates. It should equip them with the ability to understand information, organise ideas, express opinions clearly and communicate responsibly. Beyond Speaking Good English

And I always had opinions on stuff. So I think that's why I wanted to be a politician. I always had opinions on what to do, how everything should be run,” she said. stories.title: The fallen noble profession: The sad tale of the Ghanaian teacher
stories.summary: For years, it was a noble profession. To be a teacher was to be respected.

articles.title: The fallen noble profession: The sad tale of the Ghanaian teacher
articles.excerpt: For years, it was a noble profession. To be a teacher was to be respected. Today, it has become an object of ridicule. The Ghanaian teacher, who holds the future of this country in a chalk-stained hand, is now the punchline of jokes in tro-tros, markets, and family gatherings. It is a painful irony that the one who teaches others to become rich is unable to escape poverty himself.

stories.title: Digital innovation could widen Africa’s inequalities if people are left out – Sam Jonah
stories.summary: Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has warned that digital innovation could widen inequality in Africa if its benefits are concentrated among people who already have access to technology, education and economic opportunities.

articles.title: Digital innovation could widen Africa’s inequalities if people are left out – Sam Jonah
articles.excerpt: Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has warned that digital innovation could widen inequality in Africa if its benefits are concentrated among people who already have access to technology, education and economic opportunities. He said governments, universities and businesses must ensure that digital policies and platforms do not exclude people who lack reliable internet access, electricity or the resources to participate in the digital economy. “Every digital policy, every new platform, must ask a simple question: who is left out?” he said. Sir Sam was speaking at Methodist University Ghana’s international conference in Accra on Thursday, October 15, where he delivered the keynote address for the university’s 25th anniversary celebrations. He argued that a child in Dansoman with a laptop and reliable internet access has substantially different opportunities from a child in a village without electricity.

stories.title: Mfantsipim’s Musical memory gets a new lease of life in 150th Anniversary anthology
stories.summary: For 150 years, Mfantsipim School has built a legacy that extends beyond its classrooms. Its songs and hymns have accompanied generations of students, marked institutional milestones and preserved memories of people who helped shape its history.

articles.title: Mfantsipim’s Musical memory gets a new lease of life in 150th Anniversary anthology
articles.excerpt: For 150 years, Mfantsipim School has built a legacy that extends beyond its classrooms. Its songs and hymns have accompanied generations of students, marked institutional milestones and preserved memories of people who helped shape its history. Now, the Mfantsipim Old Boys Association (MOBA) has brought many of those compositions together in a 14-track collection, the Mfantsipim Sesquicentennial Anthology, launched as part of the school’s 150th anniversary celebrations. The project, recorded and produced by lawyer Ace Anan Ankomah (MOBA ’84) and sound engineer Herbert Ebenezer Crassie, combines new recordings with the reconstruction of historic works, some of which required painstaking research and recollection. Its origins were modest.

articles.title: NDC Deputy National Organizer Aspirant Hamza Umar targets grassroots mobilisation
articles.excerpt: Businessman and former student leader Hamza Umar has declared his intention to contest for Deputy National Organizer of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), pledging to strengthen grassroots participation and coordination within the party. Mr Umar, an activist from Tafo in the Ashanti Region, says his ambition is to improve collaboration between the party’s national, regional and constituency structures while ensuring that grassroots members have a stronger voice in decision-making. He previously served as President of the Local National Union of Ghana Students at the University for Development Studies (UDS) and has participated in constituency and regional campaigns within the NDC. He also contested for the position of Constituency Deputy Organizer in Tafo and currently serves on the constituency’s Financial Committee.

stories.title: Delta-BCI partnership reaches 166,000 people with breast cancer education
stories.summary: A decade-long partnership between Delta Air Lines and Breast Care International (BCI) has reached more than 166,000 people with breast cancer education in Ghana, with over 22,500 people screened and nearly 2,100 suspected cases identified.

articles.title: Delta-BCI partnership reaches 166,000 people with breast cancer education
articles.excerpt: A decade-long partnership between Delta Air Lines and Breast Care International (BCI) has reached more than 166,000 people with breast cancer education in Ghana, with over 22,500 people screened and nearly 2,100 suspected cases identified. The figures were highlighted as the two organisations marked 10 years of collaboration at the 2026 BCI Walk for the Cure in Mampong, in the Ashanti Region. The programme has also reached more than 70,100 women through targeted rural screening initiatives, as the partners work to improve access to breast cancer information and early detection. The event brought together breast cancer survivors, healthcare professionals, community leaders and thousands of participants under the theme, “Our Walk, Our Fight, Our Future”.

stories.title: Special Initiatives Minister urges Wa Technical Institute to enrol more girls as EU-backed solar training lab opens
stories.summary: Minister of State in charge of Special Initiatives at the Office of the President, Abdul-Rashid Pelpuo, has urged Wa Technical Institute to increase the enrolment of girls in renewable energy programmes, saying Ghana’s transition to green technology must create opportunities for both women and men.

articles.title: Special Initiatives Minister urges Wa Technical Institute to enrol more girls as EU-backed solar training lab opens
articles.excerpt: Minister of State in charge of Special Initiatives at the Office of the President, Abdul-Rashid Pelpuo, has urged Wa Technical Institute to increase the enrolment of girls in renewable energy programmes, saying Ghana’s transition to green technology must create opportunities for both women and men. He made the call at the launch of a solar photovoltaic (PV) training facility at the institute, established under the EU-Ghana Pact for Skills to strengthen practical training and prepare young people for jobs in the green economy. The €17 million initiative, implemented by the European Union, the International Labour Organization (ILO) and the Ghana TVET Service, seeks to bridge the gap between classroom instruction and practical skills development.

articles.excerpt: ActionAid Ghana has called for stronger measures to end child marriage and school-related abuse, urging government and community leaders to invest more in girls’ rights, education and leadership. The call was made during the 2026 International Day of the Girl-Child celebration in Techiman, Bono East Region, held under the theme “End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights.” Addressing traditional leaders, educators, students and other stakeholders, ActionAid Ghana’s Regional Programme Manager, Kwame Afram Denkyira, said girls should be recognised as rights-holders and agents of change rather than victims in need of rescue.

articles.title: UG academic calendar could collapse if GAUA strike extends into next week – Awandare
articles.excerpt: The University of Ghana’s 2026/2027 academic calendar could be severely disrupted if the ongoing strike by the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) extends into next week, Pro-Vice-Chancellor Professor Gordon Awandare has warned. Prof. Awandare said several critical university systems are currently not functioning because they are managed by GAUA members who are participating in the industrial action. “The reality is that currently many of the systems are not working because they are managed by members of GAUA who are on strike,” he said. “So the university can only do so much in terms of what we can make available in the absence of GAUA people.”

articles.title: AIT President Prof Clement Dzidonu urges lifelong learning as AI reshapes work and education
articles.excerpt: The President of the Accra Institute of Technology (AIT), Professor Clement K. Dzidonu, has called for a fundamental shift in how individuals, educational institutions and society think about learning in the age of Artificial Intelligence (AI), arguing that graduation can no longer be regarded as the end of the learning journey. Professor Dzidonu is advocating what he describes as the Sovereign Lifelong Learner — the "Sovereign Triple-L": an individual who takes ownership of continuing learning and assumes personal responsibility for continually renewing, deepening and extending their capabilities throughout professional and personal life. According to the AIT President, the traditional model in which people undergo intensive education, graduate, enter a profession and rely for many years on much of the knowledge acquired during formal education is rapidly becoming unsustainable.
